transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose I’m here because I’ve been spending rather too much time checking things at home. It’s mostly folders and drawers, and some labeled boxes where I keep important papers and little keepsakes. I’ll open them to make sure everything is where I left it, and then… even if I just looked a few minutes before, I find myself going back and checking again.

It sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud, but it’s taking up more of my day than I’d like. Is that the sort of thing you mean?

When you check your folders, drawers, or boxes, do you have specific thoughts or worries that come up for you—like a fear that something bad might happen if things aren’t in order or if you don’t check just right?

Yes… I suppose there are thoughts that come with it. I know, rationally, it’s probably all fine, but something starts needling at me—like, what if I threw away my husband’s old tax papers without meaning to, or put a family recipe in the wrong box?

It’s not that I truly think the world will end, but I get this awful feeling that I’ve been terribly careless, and I can’t quite let it go until I check. Does that make sense?
When you feel the need to check but you can’t, does it bring up a lot of anxiety or distress for you?

Yes… I think it does, though I hate to make it sound dramatic. If I can’t go back and look, it sort of sits with me and nags at me. I keep thinking about the same folder or drawer until I can check it.

That’s really why I came in, I suppose—I’m spending far too much of the day opening the same drawers and labeled boxes over and over, making sure the papers and little keepsakes are where I left them, even if I only checked a few minutes before. I know it must sound unreasonable, but it’s become hard to just leave it alone.

When you feel the urge to check your drawers or folders, does it feel like you’re trying to stop yourself from feeling anxious or prevent something bad from happening, even if you know it might not make much sense?

Yes… I think that’s right. It’s not that I can explain it terribly well, and I do know it probably doesn’t make much sense. But when the urge comes, opening the same folders or drawers or those labeled boxes again feels like the only way to settle myself.

I keep wanting to make sure the important papers and little keepsakes are still where I left them, even if I only checked a few minutes before. I’m a bit embarrassed by how much of the day it’s taking, honestly.
When you go back to check those drawers or folders, does it feel like you’re trying to get rid of a bad feeling or some discomfort, rather than just making sure things are organized or in order?

Yes… I think that’s probably fair to say. I tell myself I’m just being tidy, or careful, but really it’s more that I’m trying to quiet that awful uncomfortable feeling.

I came in because I’m spending far too much of my day opening the same folders, drawers, and labeled boxes again and again, just to make sure the important papers and little keepsakes are still where I left them—even if I only looked a few minutes earlier. I know that sounds a bit excessive, doesn’t it? But in the moment, checking seems to take the edge off.
When you feel that uncomfortable feeling before you check the drawers or folders, does it feel like you can’t relax or focus on anything else until you give in and check?

Yes… I’m afraid that’s how it feels. I try to tell myself I can just leave it, but my mind keeps going back to the drawer or the folder, and I don’t really settle until I’ve looked again.

That’s part of why I came in, really. I’m spending far too much of the day opening the same drawers and labeled boxes, checking the same papers and little keepsakes are still where I left them—even when I only checked a few minutes before. It sounds rather silly when I say it out loud, but it’s hard to focus on much else until I do it.

Are there specific thoughts or images that come into your mind that you don’t want or that feel intrusive—like something terrible happening to your family or a mistake that you might have made—something that really bothers you and you can’t seem to get rid of?

Well… yes, I suppose there are thoughts like that, though I feel a bit foolish saying it.

It’s usually not something dramatic, exactly. More like this thought keeps needling at me that I might have thrown away my husband’s old tax papers, or put a family recipe in the wrong box. Even when I know, really, that I was careful, I can’t seem to just let the thought pass. It starts to feel as if I’ve done something terribly careless, and then I feel I ought to check. Does that make sense?

When you have those troubling thoughts about possibly making a mistake with your husband’s papers or family recipes, do you feel driven to do something—like checking the drawers over and over—to try to reduce the worry or keep something bad from happening?

Yes… yes, I do think that’s what happens. I don’t like to make it sound more serious than it is, but I do feel pushed to go and look.

I’ll open the same folders or drawers, or the little labeled boxes, just to reassure myself the papers or keepsakes are still there where I left them. And sometimes I’ve only checked a few minutes before, which I know seems unreasonable… but in the moment it feels like the only way to settle the worry. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
